explain.say: Yes, a little. Every month gives 1 plus one twelfth, multiplied 12 times: about 2.613. See the third bar? Every day gives about 2.715. The bars grow, but they slow down.

explain.say: Now add it every instant, endlessly often. The total does not explode. It settles at 2.718 and a bit, the last bar. This special number is called e. It is to growth what pi is to circles.

explain.say: Well done! The Swiss mathematician Jacob Bernoulli found this in 1683, and Leonhard Euler later named it e. Today it hides in population models, loans, radio signals and the bell curve.

faq.q: Where does the number e come from?
faq.a: e is the limit of 1 plus 1 over n, all to the power n, as n grows without end. It is what 1 coin becomes at 100 percent interest added continuously for a year.

faq.q: What happens if interest is added once a year?
faq.a: At 100 percent, 1 coin becomes 1 plus 1, which is 2 coins, after one year.
Interest added at every instant, not just yearly or monthly. The money grows by a factor of e to the power rate times time.

faq.q: Why does the total stop growing at e?
faq.a: Each smaller slice of time adds a smaller piece of interest. The extra pieces shrink so fast that their total settles at a fixed value, about 2.71828.
asks: Why does more frequent compounding not give infinite money?

faq.q: Why is e used in calculus?
faq.a: e to the x is the only function, apart from multiples of it, that is its own derivative. Its slope always equals its value, so it is perfect for growth and decay.
asks: Why is the derivative of e to the x itself?

facts: e ≈ 2.71828 is the limit of (1 + 1/n)ⁿ as n tends to infinity.
Jacob Bernoulli discovered this constant in 1683 while studying compound interest.
